pr.title: Simplify `SwitchInt` handling
pr.description:
Dataflow handling of `SwitchInt` is currently complicated. This PR simplifies it.

r? @cjgillot
pr.author: nnethercote

classification.name: ElaborateDrops
evidence: The PR rewrites the shared SwitchInt edge-effect interface and the enum-discriminant tracking used by the initializedness analyses. Two concrete MIR passes consume those analyses and therefore depend on the changed behavior: ElaborateDrops uses both MaybeInitializedPlaces and MaybeUninitializedPlaces, and RemoveUninitDrops uses MaybeInitializedPlaces.

processing.reason: PR #133328 is an interface refactor, not a bug fix. The pre-PR code consumed a shared `AdtDef::discriminants` iterator with `.find(...)` once per `Some(value)` edge; the post-PR code consumes a shared `Vec` via `next_discr`, advancing one index once per `Some(value)` edge. Both map switch values to variants by the same documented ordering precondition, skip the `otherwise` (`None`) edge, and preserve the two analyses' `kill`/`gen_` effects. The supplied patch contains no regression test or changed output expectation, and the frozen analysis itself states no confirmed incorrect transformation exists. The only visible behavioral-looking discrepancy is the backward engine passing the target `block` instead of `pred` to `get_switch_int_data`, but ElaborateDrops and RemoveUninitDrops use forward analyses (`MaybeInitializedPlaces`/`MaybeUninitializedPlaces`), and no backward analysis in this patch implements `SwitchIntData`. Encoding a reset/shared-index failure or the backward-block mismatch would therefore be a fabricated rewrite rather than the historical transformation, so no source-grounded original/wrong pair can be validated under these pass IDs.

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `Analysis::apply_switch_int_edge_effects(block, discr, &mut edge_effects)` handed the analysis a callback object. `MaybeInitializedPlaces` and `MaybeUninitializedPlaces` first checked `precise_enum_drop_elaboration` (and, for the latter, `mark_inactive_variants_as_uninit`), located the enum place by scanning backwards for `_42 = discriminant(_1)` while skipping `Coverage`, created `let mut discriminants = enum_def.discriminants(self.tcx)`, and in the callback used `discriminants.find(|&(_, discr)| discr.val == value)` for each `Some(value)` edge. The callback then called `drop_flag_effects::on_all_inactive_variants` with `state.kill(mpi)` for `MaybeInitializedPlaces` or `state.gen_(mpi)` for `MaybeUninitializedPlaces`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: No confirmed incorrect transformation exists in this PR: it is a semantic-preserving interface refactor rather than a bug fix. The historical pre-PR implementation is the comparison point, not a known wrong rewrite. For test construction, the contrasting behavior is: old callback code used a continuing `discriminants.find(...)` iterator per edge, while the new code stores `MaybePlacesSwitchIntData { enum_place, discriminants, index }` and calls `next_discr(value)`, which advances a shared index and assumes edges arrive in discriminant order; a reimplementation that resets or shares this index incorrectly would select the wrong variant. No test changes are present in the supplied patch, so this is not presented as a reproduced bug.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies whose `SwitchInt` operand is the result of `Rvalue::Discriminant` on an ADT enum place (and where `Rvalue::Discriminant` may instead be for a coroutine yield point), with `precise_enum_drop_elaboration` enabled; includes enums with multiple variants and arbitrary explicit discriminants, non-enum `SwitchInt`s, and the `otherwise` edge (whose `value` is `None`). The two consuming passes are ElaborateDrops (MaybeInitializedPlaces and MaybeUninitializedPlaces) and RemoveUninitDrops (MaybeInitializedPlaces).
analysis.summary: Refactor of SwitchInt edge-effect handling shared by the initializedness analyses consumed by ElaborateDrops and RemoveUninitDrops. The key correctness invariants are discriminant-to-variant matching, flag gating, applying effects only to concrete `Some(value)` edges (not `otherwise`), and preserving the engine's edge order because `next_discr` advances a shared index.
analysis.trigger: A `SwitchInt` terminator is reached while running `MaybeInitializedPlaces` or `MaybeUninitializedPlaces` with `precise_enum_drop_elaboration` enabled, and the switch operand is a place assigned from `Rvalue::Discriminant` of an ADT enum in the same block; edge-specific effects then kill inactive-variant move paths (maybe-init) or mark them maybe-uninitialized (maybe-uninit).
preconditions: The `SwitchInt` block must contain an assignment matching `lhs == discr` from `mir::Rvalue::Discriminant(enum_place)`, ignoring `Coverage` statements.
The discriminated place's type must be `ty::Adt`; `ty::Coroutine(..)` returns `None`, and any other type is a `bug!`.
The `SwitchInt` target values must be in the same order as `AdtDef::discriminants`; `next_discr` advances through that vector using one shared index.
Only edges with `edge.value == Some(value)` receive variant effects; the `otherwise` edge has `None` and receives none.
pitfalls: Do not apply inactive-variant effects to the `otherwise` edge or to non-enum `SwitchInt`s; the code guards with `if let Some(value) = edge.value` and returns `None` from `get_switch_int_data` otherwise.
Do not reset the discriminant index per edge: `next_discr` relies on edges being processed in discriminant order and advances `self.index` each call; out-of-order calls select the wrong variant.
Do not drop the flag guards: when `precise_enum_drop_elaboration` or `mark_inactive_variants_as_uninit` is off, no edge effects should be applied.
Do not confuse the two analyses' effects: `MaybeInitializedPlaces` calls `state.kill(mpi)` for inactive variants, while `MaybeUninitializedPlaces` calls `state.gen_(mpi)`.
The documented ordering assumption is strict: the `SwitchInt` target discriminant order must match `AdtDef::discriminants`, and mismatch causes an out-of-bounds abort in `next_discr`.

In the backward direction the new engine calls `get_switch_int_data(block, discr)` while the old callback was called with `pred`; any data lookup that depends on the block layout must account for this discrepancy rather than assuming the supplied block is always the `SwitchInt`'s own block.
analysis.testStrategy: Construct MIR-level enum matches where the `SwitchInt` condition is `Rvalue::Discriminant` of an enum with several variants and explicit, non-contiguous discriminants (for example variants assigned distinct values) so target ordering and value-to-variant mapping matter. Exercise both flags on and off, and both `MaybeInitializedPlaces` and `MaybeUninitializedPlaces` consumers: partially initialize different enum variants in match arms, give fields drop types with observable side effects, and compare drop behavior/elimination between the old callback logic and the new `next_discr` indexing implementation. Also include a non-enum `SwitchInt`, a coroutine yield discriminant, and an `otherwise` arm to verify that no variant effects are applied there. Check MIR for `_x = discriminant(_place)` immediately before `SwitchInt`. Do not claim runtime reproduction without building the compiler; the supplied patch contains no regression test changes.
